task: SCS-001 Slices 1-3 — Submission Read, Teacher Submission Discovery (Issue #20), Teacher Submission Review (Issue #24)

invariants: L-001 every assignment and submission has exactly one data owner
L-002 a subject of Tenant A never reaches Learning data of Tenant B, including by changing submission_id or a caller-supplied tenant_id
L-003 a request with an IS-003 DENY never reaches the owned-data operation
L-004 an authorization dependency failure or a malformed/non-authoritative dependency answer fails closed to DENY
L-005 the effective tenant comes from IS-001; this component creates no second tenant-context mechanism
L-006 the public surface provides no access path that bypasses the Learning enforcement boundary
L-007 security-sensitive refusals are auditable and observable with request/correlation and actor/tenant context where applicable
L-008 the internals of this component are not a consumer contract: a consumer receives the published client and values only
L-009 a list answer contains only submissions of the requested Assignment, or is a refusal — there is no partial cross-assignment or cross-tenant set

operations.purpose: serve one owned submission after the enforcement chain allowed the access
operations.idempotency_note: A read changes no state beyond the append-only audit journal.

operations.purpose: list one Assignment's submissions after the enforcement chain allowed the access (teacher discovery); an empty assignment answers 200 with {items: []}
operations.idempotency_note: A read changes no state beyond the append-only audit journal.

operations.purpose: record that a teacher has checked one owned submission; sets reviewed_by and reviewed_at and leaves the lifecycle SUBMITTED
operations.idempotency_note: State-changing command guarded by IS-005: the Idempotency-Key header is mandatory, an exact replay returns the recorded result without a second effect, and a changed binding is refused as IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.

enforcement_model.passed_through_denials: the published deny reasons of IS-003, unchanged
enforcement_model.nonauthoritative_answers: an answer outside the published decision model of IS-003 — including an ALLOW with a reason other than permitted and a DENY with an unknown reason — fails closed as authorization_unavailable

review.semantics: review records the fact that a submission has been checked: reviewed_by (verified teacher identity) and reviewed_at (timestamp) are set on the first successful review, remain immutable thereafter, and the lifecycle stays SUBMITTED. Review is not grading, scoring, feedback, commenting, evaluation or a lifecycle transition.
review.state_rule: review is allowed only when status == SUBMITTED; a DRAFT submission is refused as invalid_state_transition
review.immutability: reviewed_by and reviewed_at are set by the first successful review and are immutable thereafter: a review command with a different Idempotency-Key against an already reviewed submission is refused as already_reviewed and never overwrites the first review fact
review.idempotency: IS-005 guard; Idempotency-Key mandatory; exact replay returns the recorded result; changed binding is refused as idempotency_conflict. The two cases stay distinct: same key = idempotent replay, different key = a new command against an immutable review fact
review.no_review_entity: no Review, Evaluation, Grade, Feedback or LearningResult entity exists; the review fact is exactly the two nullable fields reviewed_by / reviewed_at on Submission

refusal_semantics.principle: a refusal is data with a stable machine-readable code and reason, audited with request_id and correlation_id; nothing about this surface can be mistaken for a served submission

error.message: the stable message of the code

shape.request_id: the request_id the refusal was audited with
shape.correlation_id: the correlation_id the refusal was audited with

AUTHORIZATION_DENIED.reasons: tenant_mismatch, tenant_unknown, platform_ownership_mismatch, resource_tenant_unknown, resource_tenant_mismatch, tenant_not_active, tenant_suspended, tenant_deletion_requested, tenant_deleted, permission_not_granted, authority_unavailable, missing_tenant_context, owner_mismatch

INVALID_REQUEST.message: Request does not match the published contract.
INVALID_REQUEST.note: defence in depth: the schema handler exists, but the read surface carries no body, so no live 422 scenario exists in this slice

INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION.message: Operation is not valid for the current submission state.

ALREADY_REVIEWED.message: The submission has already been reviewed.

IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED.message: An Idempotency-Key header is required for this operation.

IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.message: The Idempotency-Key was already used with a different request.

envelope.note: The HTTP status selects the code; the stable internal reason is preserved in error.details.reason; request_id and correlation_id match the audit record of the refusal.

refused.403: tenant_mismatch, tenant_unknown, platform_ownership_mismatch, resource_tenant_unknown, resource_tenant_mismatch, tenant_not_active, tenant_suspended, tenant_deletion_requested, tenant_deleted, permission_not_granted, authority_unavailable, missing_tenant_context, owner_mismatch

refusal_semantics.served: HTTP 200 with the ten-field submission representation (including reviewed_by / reviewed_at) — one submission or {items: [...]} — produced only by the owned-data operation at the end of the enforcement chain

consumer_surface.transport: learning_service.transport.open_channel + learning_service.transport.call_contract — the published HTTP contract executed in process over an opaque channel handle (ARCHITECTURE.md §1.1 interaction mode API, Level 0)
errors: learning_service.errors.AccessRefused — the access did not happen; the reason is one of the published refusal reasons (401/403/404/503), carried in error.details.reason, with the request_id/correlation_id of the refusal
learning_service.errors.ContractViolation — the contract transport failed or answered outside its published shape (including any non-envelope shape); a consumer must fail closed
guarantees: values only: no learning store, audit journal, engine reference or deployment is reachable through the published surface
the published client holds no callable and no credential: its state is one channel handle, so walking the client and its class reaches neither the component's ASGI application nor its internals
the subject credential is supplied per access and verified by IS-001 inside the IS-003 decision: a consumer cannot assert who the subject is
the ASGI application is never handed out: it stays behind the provider-side channel table, and a channel is revoked when the consumer drops the client
importing the published module binds no reference to learning_service.transport — its namespace holds no module object, no channel table and no transport type
an unknown or revoked channel handle raises ContractViolation, so there is no permissive fallback and a handle cannot be guessed
every access runs through the same routing, enforcement chain and audit code that serves an HTTP request

there is no assignment listing, bulk export, search, pagination or raw-store operation beyond the published per-assignment list: the two published reads and the review command are the only access paths, and all of them are enforced
the review command owns no second idempotency mechanism: it is delivered to the IS-005 guard, which decides between executing, replaying and refusing a conflict
composition_root_only: the contract application itself (the ASGI application) — a consumer component must not own or re-export it
the contract channel table learning_service.transport._CHANNELS — a handle-to-application mapping owned by the component
consumer_surface.note: The deployment object is composition-internal: it assembles engine, store and contract application for the composition root and for this component's own tests and is never handed to a consumer. This component composes no other component and publishes no module-level demo application: a demo of a data owner needs a composed Platform Instance with a live decision dependency, and composing one is the job of a composition root.

consumes.mechanism: contract client over the published API of authorization, executed in process at Level 0
consumes.credential_source: deployment secret resolved by the composition root: the service identity of this component
consumes.note: The access decision is read per access and never cached. The resource's owning Tenant stated in the question comes from this component's own store, never from a caller claim (LAW-16a). The single-read question names the submission, the teacher-discovery question names the Assignment; both name the record's own tenant from the store.
consumes.dependency_isolation: No module of learning imports authorization_service, identity_service or tenant_authority: the published client is adapted at the composition boundary and only values owned by this component reach the enforcement logic (ARCHITECTURE.md 1.1, 6.1, LAW-04).

events.note: SCS-001 Slices 1-3 publish no inter-component events and do not simulate a broker. The access audit journal is owned data, not a public event contract.

data_export_cdc.note: No CDC or bulk export stream is implemented in Slices 1-3. A bulk path would be a bypass risk for the enforcement boundary and is deliberately out of this slice.

ui.note: Class A Business System / SCS; UI is out of this Level 0 slice. Every published read is proven at the API boundary.

platform_id.description: Identifier of the Platform Instance this data owner serves.

datasets.name: assignments
datasets.note: Every assignment has exactly one data owner (owner_component) and belongs to exactly one Tenant; ownership is registered explicitly and cannot be redefined.

datasets.name: submissions
datasets.note: Every submission belongs to exactly one assignment and to the same Tenant; student_identity_id is an opaque reference — no student profile/account data is stored here. reviewed_by / reviewed_at are opaque review facts set by the first successful review and immutable thereafter; no Review/Evaluation/Grade/Feedback/LearningResult entity exists.

datasets.name: access_audit
datasets.note: Append-only journal of every access attempt — served or refused — with request/correlation and actor/tenant context where known.

notes: This component owns no identity, no permission grant, no tenant registry and no tenant state: those belong to identity, authorization and tenant_authority and are read through their published contracts.

The submission model is the business model of Slices 1-3 (submission_id, assignment_id, student_identity_id, attempt, content, status, created_at, updated_at, reviewed_by, reviewed_at) with lifecycle DRAFT → SUBMITTED; no grading, comments, review states, progress or enrollment exist. Review is exactly the fact that a submitted submission was checked, recorded in the two nullable review fields.

audit.journal: internal append-only journal owned by learning
audit.refusal_audit_scope: every refusal of the published contract, including a request rejected by the contract schema before any handler runs and a refusal produced because the decision dependency did not answer; the record carries request_id and correlation_id of the caller
audit.note: Audit is owned data, not a public event contract, and is not readable through the published surface.

observability.saga_id: absent — this component runs no inter-component sagas

authn.note: The subject credential presented on the public surface is verified by IS-001 inside the IS-003 decision; this component verifies no credential itself. When asking IS-003, this component authenticates with its own service identity (demo: authz-svc-token-learning).

authz.note: ALLOW from IS-003 is not direct data access: the data owner remains the final enforcement boundary (ARCHITECTURE.md §6.2). A decision that cannot be obtained is a denial. A Teacher must hold learning.submissions.review to review and learning.submissions.list to discover submissions of an Assignment; a Student and every other subject without an explicit grant is denied by default.

compatibility_policy.reason_codes: adding a refusal reason is a minor change; removing or redefining one is a breaking change
compatibility_policy.enforcement_chain: reordering or removing a step is a breaking change: the order is part of the published behaviour
compatibility_policy.resource_model: adding a field to the submission representation is a minor change; changing the ten published fields is a breaking change
compatibility_policy.error_envelope: the approved envelope shape is part of the contract; changing error/code/message/details/request_id/correlation_id is a breaking change
compatibility_policy.lifecycle: submission lifecycle is exactly DRAFT → SUBMITTED; adding grading/review states is a breaking change; review does not add a lifecycle state

dependencies.direction: learning -> idempotency_guard (exactly-once delivery of the review command)
dependencies.note: SCS-001 implements no second idempotency mechanism: the review command identity (operation, target, fingerprint) is delivered to IS-005, which decides between executing, replaying and refusing a conflict.
